launchPhaseDetail: Issued by RD InnoTech Limited (a subsidiary of RD Technologies, founded by former HKMA chief executive Norman Chan); admitted to the HKMA stablecoin issuer sandbox in the first July 2024 cohort. Raised $40M in Series A2 (July 30 2025, led by ZA Global) and signed a Memorandum of Understanding with ZA Bank for HKDR reserve custody and potential distribution pending regulatory approval — the first major collaboration between a licensed HK virtual bank and a stablecoin development company. Hong Kong Stablecoins Ordinance took effect August 1 2025; 36 formal applications were received by the September deadline. HKMA granted its first two stablecoin licences on April 10 2026 to Anchorpoint Financial (FRS01) and HSBC (FRS02) — RD InnoTech was not in the first batch. HSBC plans its HKD stablecoin launch for H2 2026; a second licence wave is expected and RD InnoTech, with its early sandbox participation, $40M war chest, and ZA Bank partnership, remains among the credible next-round candidates. HK$25M minimum paid-up capital and 100%+ reserve backing requirements already met under sandbox conditions.

launchPhaseDetail: Pilot phase following successful September 2025 proof of concept; not yet in public circulation. BDACS is South Korea's regulated digital-asset custodian; Woori Bank holds the won reserves and participated directly in the PoC. Initial deployment on Avalanche (cited by KISA for reliability in public-sector use); KRW1 expanded to Polygon in December 2025 for broader payments, remittances, and enterprise reach. October 2025 MoU with Circle positions KRW1 for deployment on Arc (Circle's new Layer 1), where it joins national stablecoin issuers from Japan, Brazil, Mexico, and the Philippines. February 2026 Plume partnership positions KRW1 as Korean institutional settlement rail for tokenized RWA. May 2026 Aptos Foundation partnership brings KRW1 to its first non-EVM chain, leveraging Aptos's payment infrastructure for cross-border remittances and RWA tokenisation. The Bank of Korea nominee (April 2026) signalled CBDC and bank-issued deposit tokens should lead Korea's digital money system, with private stablecoins in a secondary role — a headwind for commercial launch timing. Commercial launch contingent on Korea's forthcoming Digital Asset Basic Act framework.

launchPhaseDetail: Companion to the already-tracked RGBP (Revolut GBP). Revolut secured a MiCA CASP licence from Cyprus (CySEC) on Oct 23 2025 and operates an existing EMI licence in Lithuania — the legal foundations for issuing e-money tokens under MiCA Title IV. In October 2025, Revolut launched fee-free 1:1 USD↔stablecoin swaps (USDC/USDT on Ethereum, Solana, and Tron) for its 65M users; stablecoin payment volumes on the platform surged 156% in 2025 to ~$10.5B. In February 2026, the FCA selected Revolut as one of 4 firms (from 20 applicants) for a UK stablecoin payment testing pilot covering payments, wholesale settlement, and crypto trading — results will inform the FCA's crypto framework targeting October 2027. A Revolut-branded proprietary USD stablecoin has not been officially confirmed; Polymarket puts the probability at ~25% by year-end 2026. Specific ticker, chain selection, and reserve disclosure model remain unannounced.

obituary.obituary: Nerite built USND on immutable Liquity V2-style contracts, but one of its approved collateral branches depended on rsETH. After the rsETH hack impaired that collateral, Nerite could not simply patch the market away or rewrite the risk controls. Supply collapsed from a $2.7M peak to under $100K, leaving USND as an archived case study in how immutable CDP systems can still inherit external collateral failure when a supported asset breaks upstream.

obituary.epitaph: When one key minted eighty million
obituary.obituary: On 22 March 2026, an attacker exploited Resolv's single-EOA minter — no oracle, no amount cap, no max-mint guard — depositing 100K USDC and receiving 50M USR in return, then iterating until 80M unbacked USR existed for ~$25M of extracted ETH. USR crashed to $0.025 in 17 minutes; the RLP insurance layer absorbed the bad debt and was wiped out, dragging Stream Finance's $17M position down with it. Resolv burned 46M of the unbacked supply via a blacklist freeze, but USR never recovered — by April it traded at $0.16 with $95M of collateral against $173M of liabilities. Delta-neutral collateral and Apostro-attested reserves were no defense against an operator-level privilege failure.
